In [[mathematical physics]], the '''Eckhaus equation''' – or the '''Kundu–Eckhaus equation''' – is a nonlinear [[partial differential equation]] within the [[nonlinear Schrödinger equation|nonlinear Schrödinger]] class:<ref>{{harvtxt|Zwillinger|1998|pp=177 & 390}}</ref>

:<math>i \psi_t + \psi_{xx} +2 \left( |\psi|^2 \right)_x\, \psi + |\psi|^4\, \psi = 0.</math>

The equation was independently introduced by [[Wiktor Eckhaus]] and by Anjan Kundu to model the propagation of [[wave]]s in [[dispersion (optics)|dispersive media]].<ref>{{harvtxt|Eckhaus|1985}}</ref><ref>{{harvtxt|Kundu|1984}}</ref>

==Linearization==
[[File:Eckhaus equation wave packet.gif|right|thumb|480px|Animation of a [[Wave packet|wave-packet]] solution of the Eckhaus equation. The blue line is the [[complex number|real part]] of the solution, the red line is the [[complex number|imaginary part]] and the black line is the [[Envelope (waves)|wave envelope]] ([[absolute value]]). Note the [[symmetry|asymmetry]] in the envelope <math>|\psi(x,t)|</math> for the Eckhaus equation, while the envelope <math>|\varphi(x,t)|</math> – of the corresponding solution to the linear Schrödinger equation – is symmetric (in <math>x</math>). The short waves in the packet propagate faster than the long waves.]]
[[File:Schrödinger_equation_wave_packet.gif|thumb|right|480px|Animation of the [[:en:Wave packet|wave-packet]] solution of the [[:en:Schrödinger equation|linear Schrödinger equation]] – corresponding with the above animation for the Eckhaus equation. The blue line is the [[:en:complex number|real part]] of the solution, the red line is the [[:en:complex number|imaginary part]], the black line is the [[:en:Envelope (waves)|wave envelope]] ([[:en:Absolute value|absolute value]]) and the green line is the [[centroid]] of the wave packet envelope.]]
The Eckhaus equation can be [[linearization|linearized]] to the [[Schrödinger equation|linear Schrödinger equation]]:<ref>{{harvtxt|Calogero|De Lillo|1987}}</ref>

:<math>i \varphi_t + \varphi_{xx} =0,</math>

through the non-linear transformation:<ref>{{harvtxt|Ablowitz|Ahrens|De Lillo|2005}}</ref>

:<math>\varphi(x,t) = \psi(x,t)\, \exp\left( \int_{-\infty}^x |\psi(x^\prime,t)|^2\; \text{d}x^\prime \right).</math>

The inverse transformation is:

:<math>\psi(x,t) = \frac{\varphi(x,t)}{\displaystyle \left( 1 + 2\, \int_{-\infty}^x |\varphi(x^\prime,t)|^2\; \text{d}x^\prime \right)^{1/2}}.</math>

This linearization also implies that the Eckhaus equation is [[integrable system|integrable]].
